title: Turn Slab Economy — PRD seed and experiments scratchpad
body:
Quick seed for an experiment+mini-PRD exploring a per-turn compute "economy" concept (working name: "Turn Slab").

Goal (one-liner):
Provide a lightweight, auditable mechanism for applications to trade per-turn output fidelity versus cost/latency by selecting a "slab" policy per request that the runtime can honor with model variant selection, quantization hints, and batching/caching behavior.

Why this matter (problem):
- Many apps have variable per-turn needs inside a single session (e.g., short confirmations, search queries, long-form composition). Currently the app picks one model/config per session or route which wastes tokens or latency.
- Existing fallback knobs are coarse (global routing, model rollouts). We need a compact surface that product SDKs and UIs can use to indicate expected value of a single turn.
- This helps customers reduce unit cost while maintaining UX SLOs and gives Redwood observable levers to route/batch more effectively.

High-level concept:
- Turn = one user+system prompt -> one response. Attach a "slab" metadata token that indicates desired compute tier for this turn. Slabs are small enums (e.g., micro|standard|premium) plus optional numeric budget hint (token budget/time budget).
- Runtime translates slab -> concrete serving plan: model family (tiny/medium/large), quantization level, max KV reuse window, batching latency target, and fallback policy (if capacity constrained fall back to compatible slab).
- API: client sets slab per request (header, SDK param). If not set, route uses default per-route slab.

Goals / Success metrics:
- 20–40% reduction in average cost per token for apps that adopt slab hints on non-critical turns.
- <5% increase in error/regression rate for critical e2e intents (measured via eval hooks).
- Latency SLOs: premium slabs meet current p95 targets; micro slabs trade latency for cost (p95 may be slightly higher but still bounded).

User stories (examples):
- As a chat app developer, I want quick yes/no confirmations to use micro slab so users get fast and cheap answers.
- As a search assistant, I want short factual lookups to use standard slab and long explanation turns to use premium automatically.
- As an enterprise customer, I want per-turn slab annotations to be honored in Dedicated instances to respect cost tiers and auditing.

Proposed API surface (sketch):
- request param: slab: oneOf [micro, standard, premium, custom]
- optional: slab_token_budget: integer (max tokens to spend on model output)
- optional: slab_compute_hint: freeform string (e.g., "prefer-quantized" or "prefer-kv-reuse") for future features
- server response metadata: served_slab: string, model_variant: string, estimated_cost_units: float

Runtime translation examples (mapping table, rough):
- micro -> small open model (quantized 4bit), aggressive KV reuse (reuse across recent turns even if short), batching window=50ms, max tokens=64
- standard -> medium model, 8-bit quant for edge GPUs or float16 on high-end, batching=100ms, max tokens=256
- premium -> high-fidelity model (float16/float32), no quantization, batching=20ms (low latency), max tokens=1024

Quality controls and safety:
- Attach opt-in eval hooks: when a slab-level change reduces quality for a tracked prompt set, fire regression alert.
- Default safety: premium slab must still run through content filters; micro slab uses lighter heuristics but preserves blocklist checks.
- Auditing: log slab chosen and model_variant served for billing and compliance.

Experiments to validate:
1) A/B: route 50% of small-turns with slab micro vs baseline standard. Measure cost, end-user completion (via telemetry), and any increase in follow-up clarifications.
2) Heuristic auto-suggestion: train cheap classifier in SDK to tag turns likely safe for micro slab (based on length, punctuation, intent). Evaluate precision/recall and UX impact.
3) Cache impact: measure how KV reuse aggressiveness for micro slab influences downstream token re-generation and latency.

Telemetry & instrumentation needs: 
- Per-turn recorded: client_slab_hint, served_slab, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_in/tokens_out, followup_probability (did user send immediate follow-up within 10s), quality_score (if we can compute).
- Rollup dashboards: cost-per-slab, p95 latency per-slab per-model, rate of slab-fallback events, slab->model mismatch frequency.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0: internal alpha for Redwood apps + SDKs with opt-in. Gather telemetry and refine mapping.
- Phase 1: public beta (hosted API) with slab param documented. Start with micro/standard only.
- Phase 2: add premium, custom slabs, and Dedicated controls (policy enforcement).

Edge cases / open questions (TODO list):
- How to enforce slab behaviour in Dedicated where customers may want to ignore cost hints? (policy negotiation + enterprise flag?)
- What are good default mappings across hardware types (A100 vs H100 vs edge)?
- Billing impact: do we bill by served model_variant or by slab-defined price? (Simpler: bill by served model_variant but provide slab usage breakout).
- How to prevent abuse (e.g., gaming slab hints to force premium variants)? Need server-side validation and quotas.
- Should slab hint influence streaming behavior (e.g., micro slab should still stream tokens as they come)?

Design notes / UX ideas: 
- SDK convenience: auto-slab heuristics that surface to app devs with SW toggle.
- Console: slab usage per-route chart + annotation that shows cost savings if switched.
- Guide: short cookbook describing typical slab patterns for chat, search, summarization.

Next steps (short):
- Prototype mapping in runtime simulator (perf/cost model) — infra + applied-ml pairing.
- Add minimal slab param to Hosted API prototype and run a 1-week A/B with internal traffic.
- Draft public docs + FAQ that explain expected quality tradeoffs and billing model.

Notes: this is intentionally small surface: enum + token budget. The power is that the runtime can optimize (model selection, quantization, batching) without app devs understanding internals. Keep surface tight to encourage adoption.

Open followups for collaborators:
- Mika: can you scope the runtime simulator inputs we need? (cost per model variant, latency curves, kv-hit rate assumptions)
- Nora: can you draft two example SDK heuristics (JS/Python) to auto-suggest slabs?
- Ethan: can infra estimate logging volume and cost for per-turn telemetry?

Random brain dump / fringe ideas:
- Time-decayed slab: client marks a turn as "transient micro" meaning subsequent turns may inherit micro unless overwritten. Helps short confirmation bursts.
- Negative slabs: "economy-negative" that forces extra validation on safety-critical prompts.
- Delegated slab authority: enterprise customers can define allowed slab sets per API key.

-- end of seed scratchpad --
